title: Other compositions and writing with Lunceford
summary: He describes "Easy Does It," a song for Billie Holiday, "Traveling Light" as his best melody, and Lunceford's encouragement.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: One Sunday out in Nashville. He and I wrote several little things together then. I left the -- he left the band. I started writing a few little things on my own, and I -- the first thing I wrote when he left was "What's you know, Joe", that little tune. I used to like to write little catchy phrases like that, you know. I did another song for Billie Holiday just before she died but -- and she liked it

but she wasn't in no shape to sing it then. And I've never done anything with the tune since. I wrote it with a guy in Honolulu there, Andy Cummings. But maybe later on I'll try to do something. It's called "Riff-raff", you know. Cute little tune but we never did -- she liked it but she was in no shape then when I last saw her.
But I used to like to write. I did a lot of composition.
What are your other? I mean I guess I know--

Well, "Easy does it". You probably know that (hums a few measures). That's my tune. Sy and I wrote that together. I don't know. I can't -- some -- but a lot of them wasn't -- didn't get popular -- that you wouldn't have really known. Some of them did, you know. But the best -- I think the best thing I ever did was that "Traveling Light". I think it's the best thing I ever did. I didn't write the lyrics for it but I liked the melody.

All the guys that knew I wrote it back -- they loved the melody -- way back, you know. But that's about the best melody that I ever wrote -- that I ever did. Once in a while you can come up with a -- you can't do that -- I can't -- consistently, you know. But once in a while you really strike a haunting melody that appeals to a lot of people, you know. You can't -- I don't think anybody can do it all the time, but some guys can do it more consistently than others. But I
couldn't. I haven't been back into writing but I want to get back into it now.

Yeah, I want to. I really want to get back. But with Lunceford I had a lot of incentive to do things because everybody over there was on their toes and trying to do something, you know. And it was -- I don't know -- I really wanted to move when I was with Lunceford. I really wanted to do a lot of things, and Lunceford was encouraging. You know, naturally because some of the tunes he was putting with his publishing company. So, naturally he would want -- he would want them going, you know.
